chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The small bird (qubbara), the medium bird (sa'wa), and the sparrow (asfuru), if the person in ihram kills them, then upon him is a mud of food for each one of them. And whoever kills a lizard, then upon him is a kaf of food, as narrated.

key_terms.الصَّعْوَةُ: A medium-sized bird, distinct from the small and large categories.
key_terms.الْعُصْفُورُ: The sparrow, a common small bird.
key_terms.الْقُبَّرَةُ: A type of small bird, often identified as the quail or similar small game.
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: A pilgrim who has entered the state of ihram.
key_terms.عَظَايَةً: A lizard, specifically the monitor lizard or similar species found in the Hijaz.
key_terms.كَفٌّ: A specific volume measure for food, typically larger than a mud.
key_terms.مُدٌّ: A specific volume measure for food, approximately 0.75 liters.

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation (kaffarah) for killing small birds or lizards while in ihram during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific fidya (expiation) for a pilgrim in ihram who accidentally kills small game, distinguishing between minor birds and reptiles. It establishes a graded penalty system where small birds incur a mud of food per bird, while a lizard requires a kaf, reflecting the juristic principle of proportionality in compensating for the sanctity of the pilgrimage state.
